recommendation_summary: Right now: run a new Ethernet cable to the desk computer on a path the grommet won't crush, then place a test call. Nothing optional is added. It says outright not to buy the UniFi gateway, managed switches or Grafana. It doesn't address the future-proofing wish, apart from deleting that stack as a current requirement, and it gives no fallback if the new cable doesn't fix the drops.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Dependable video calls at one desk (you). You also asked for a UniFi gateway, managed switches, and Grafana because a home-network group uses them and you want to future-proof.
labels.Deleted: UniFi gateway, managed switches, and a Grafana dashboard. This failure gives no reason to add gear you must run and watch.
labels.Bottleneck: The several-year-old desk Ethernet cable through a tight grommet. A different cable has not been tried, while two other devices on the same router keep their calls.
labels.Checked myself: You said the desk computer uses Ethernet, those two devices stayed connected during a dropout, the cable is old and passes a tight grommet, and you have not tried another cable.

note: Bounded fix (replace the cable, then test a call); the stack is named and deleted; all four record lines come first and rest on facts the user supplied.
